transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I, um... I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. I'm mainly here because of some things going on at work. I'm a translator, and... well, I really don't want to sound like a difficult employee or like I'm just complaining, but for months now, I’ve been seeing this same pattern in our project files. 

It's just that... certain subcontractors and one colleague in particular keep making these tiny little changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. It's done in a way that makes it look like my quality control failed. I actually asked IT to look into it, just to be sure, and they told me the audit trail is completely clean. I didn't push it with them because I really don't want to cause a problem at the office, but... I just know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

Does that make sense? I hope I don't sound unreasonable for being so worried about it, I just wasn't sure who else to talk to. Is it okay that I came in for this?
Even after IT told you the audit trail was clean, are you still certain your colleague is arranging the records to make you look at fault?

I know it probably sounds a bit... much. And I really don't want to be the guy who thinks he knows better than the IT department. They do good work, and I'd never want to insult them. But... yes, doctor, I am. I'm still certain. 

It's just that I've been doing this job for years, and I know my own files. Even if the official audit trail looks completely clean to them, I can still see the pattern. Those little adjustments to the translation memory... the timestamps... they're just too perfectly placed to make my quality control look bad. I think the records have just been arranged really, really carefully by my colleague so it doesn't leave an obvious trace for IT to find. 

I'm sorry, I hope I don't sound completely stubborn or... or paranoid for saying that. I really don't want to be difficult. Do you think it's understandable that I'd still be worried, given what I'm seeing on my end?
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I... I really hope I didn't give you the impression that I'm, um, hearing things or losing touch like that. It's really just the actual files on my computer that I'm looking at. I haven't heard any voices or anything. 

I'm sorry if I made it sound like my mind was playing tricks on me. I know my concerns about the office probably sound a little intense, so I completely understand why you'd need to ask that. But no, nothing like that. Is that a good sign, at least? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and not making this more complicated than it needs to be.
Apart from this issue at work, do you believe anyone else is trying to harm, monitor, or plot against you?

No, no, nothing like that. It's really just this one specific situation at work. I don't think anyone else is out to get me or watching me or anything. I have a really nice life outside of the office, actually. My neighbors are great, my friends are supportive... I really don't have any problems with anyone else. 

I just... I really want to make sure you know I'm not a suspicious person by nature. I try to get along with everyone, and I usually do! It's just this one colleague and the files... that's the only thing that's been bothering me. I hope that makes sense? I really don't want you to think I'm just paranoid about everyone around me, because I promise I'm not. Is it okay that it's just this one specific thing?
How long have you been certain that your colleague is arranging the records to make you look at fault?

Well, I guess it's been... um... it's been a little while. I really hope you don't think I'm the type of person who just holds onto things or looks for problems, because I promise I'm really not. But, um... it's been about 11 months. 

It started shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project at work. I tried to just ignore it at first and give them the benefit of the doubt, to be a good team player, you know? I really hate causing a fuss or making anyone uncomfortable. I just kept hoping it was a misunderstanding and that it would stop. 

Is it... is it okay that I've been noticing it for that long? I hope it doesn't make me look bad for not bringing it up sooner. I just really didn't want to be a bother to anyone or make a big deal out of it until I was absolutely sure.
Have you had any neurological illness or head injury?

Oh, no. No, definitely not. I've never had any head injuries or... or any kind of neurological illnesses. I've always been very healthy in that regard, actually. I try to take really good care of myself, and I haven't been in any accidents or anything like that. 

Um... I hope that's helpful for your notes? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information. I promise my memory and my physical health are perfectly fine, so I hope that makes your evaluation a little easier. Is there anything else about my medical history you need me to clarify? I'm happy to answer whatever you need.
Outside of this work issue, have you become less interested in seeing friends or doing your usual activities?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I really hope I'm not giving the impression that I'm, you know, falling apart or shutting down. I'm actually doing really well with everything else! 

Outside of that one project issue, I still do all my regular translating work, I manage my team's workflow just fine, I pay my bills on time... I'm still keeping up with all my family routines, too. I still love seeing my friends and doing the things I normally enjoy. I really try to stay on top of my responsibilities, and I think I do a good job of it. 

It's really only... well, the only place things ever get a little off track is just when the file history or those certain coworkers come up. But everything else is completely normal and fine. I hope that shows that I'm still functioning well? I just want to reassure you that I'm handling my life properly, aside from that one little hiccup at the office. Does that sound okay to you?
Before this problem at work began, have you generally tended to distrust other people’s motives?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've always prided myself on being a very trusting person, actually. I really believe in, you know, seeing the best in people and working together. I've never been the type to be suspicious or hold grudges, I promise. 

Before this whole... situation with the localization project, I had wonderful relationships with everyone at the office, and I still do with most people! I've always gotten along fine with my colleagues and friends. I really hope you don't think I'm just a paranoid person who goes around looking for reasons to distrust people, because that's not me at all. I try very hard to be agreeable and easy to work with. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure you know that this isn't some lifelong personality flaw of mine or anything like that. It's really just this one specific thing that's been happening lately.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts were being controlled or influenced by someone else?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I've never felt anything like that. That sounds... well, that sounds very frightening, actually, but no, my thoughts are completely my own. 

I've always had a very clear mind, which is so important for translating, you know? You really have to be sharp and in control of your own words and thoughts. So, no, nobody is putting thoughts in my head or controlling me or anything like that. I'm completely in charge of my own mind, I assure you. 

I really hope that's the right answer? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the wrong idea about how my mind works. I'm very grounded in reality, I promise. Does that help clear things up for your assessment?
Has anyone told you that your speech or your thoughts seem confused or hard to follow?

Oh, no, no one has ever said anything like that to me. I really try to be as clear and articulate as possible, especially given my line of work. Communication is everything in translation, you know? 

I always make a point to organize my thoughts before I speak, and I think people generally find me very easy to understand. I've never had anyone tell me I'm confusing or that I'm not making sense. I hope I've been clear with you today, too? I really want to make sure I'm giving you good, helpful answers. I'm doing my best to be as straightforward as I can. Does my speech seem okay to you?
Have you found yourself showing much less emotion on your face or in your voice than you used to?

Oh, no, I don't think so at all. Um, actually, I'd say I'm quite an expressive person. In my line of work—especially when I'm doing live interpreting—you really have to convey the tone and feeling behind the words, you know? So having a flat voice or a blank face would... well, it would make me pretty bad at my job! 

I always try to be warm and engaged when I'm talking to people. I certainly haven't noticed any changes like that, and no one has mentioned anything to me. I mean, I hope I don't come across as cold or emotionless right now? I really try my best to be pleasant and responsive with everyone. Do I seem okay to you in that regard?
Is it possible in real life for your colleague to alter those records without IT being able to detect it?

Well, um, I know it sounds a bit... unusual, I suppose. And I really don't want to come across as difficult or, or paranoid—I know how that sounds. But yes, I do believe it's possible. 

I mean, I'm here because for months now, I've been seeing this same pattern in our project files. It’s just these tiny, tiny changes, you know? Certain subcontractors and this one colleague, they keep altering the translation memory and the timestamps. It's done in a way that makes it look like my quality control failed. And, well, even when IT says the audit trail is clean and they can't find anything, I just... I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

I really try to be a team player, I do, and I hate even bringing this up because I want to be easy to work with. But the pattern is just so clear to me. I hope I'm explaining this in a way that makes sense? I'm not trying to cause trouble, I just want to do my job well. Does that seem like a reasonable concern to have, given the circumstances?
Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

Oh, no, definitely not. I've never had any... well, any hallucinations or anything like that. I know that's something doctors have to ask about, but I promise my eyes are perfectly fine. 

I mean, the things I'm noticing at work, they're right there on the screen in the files, you know? It's not something I'm just imagining or seeing out of nowhere. I've always had very good vision—I kind of have to, staring at documents all day. I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm seeing things that aren't there. I'm very grounded in reality, I really am. I hope that puts your mind at ease? I'm trying to be as honest and helpful as possible.
Do you believe your colleague has any impossible or supernatural way of changing the records without IT being able to detect it?

Oh, no, no, nothing like that. Um, I don't believe in anything supernatural or... or impossible. I know how that might sound, and I really don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. 

I just think they're very, very good with computers. Maybe they know a workaround or some sort of backdoor in the software that IT just hasn't caught onto yet? People figure out ways to get around firewalls and things all the time, right? It's just a technical thing, nothing magical. I really hope I'm not coming across as, well, crazy for thinking that? I'm just trying to make sense of what I'm seeing in the files in a logical way. Does that sound like a reasonable explanation to you?
Have you ever had a period when your thoughts felt jumbled or confused?

Oh, um, no. No, my thoughts are usually very clear. I mean, I have to be sharp for my work, translating and keeping track of all the details. I don't really get confused or... or jumbled up. 

I mean, I might get a little stressed sometimes, like anyone would, especially with everything going on at the office right now. But my mind is working just fine, I promise. I really try to stay organized and focused. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to reassure you that I'm thinking completely straight.
Have you ever felt that someone was controlling your actions or movements?

Oh, no, absolutely not. I... I've never felt like a puppet or anything like that. I'm always the one in charge of what I do. 

I know sometimes people with, um, mental health struggles might feel that way, but I promise I'm completely in control of my own actions. I make my own choices, go where I want to go, do what I need to do. It's just the files at work that are being messed with, not me. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my grip on myself. I'm very independent. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.

I always try to be warm and engaged when I'm talking to people. I certainly haven't noticed any changes like that, and no one has mentioned anything to me. I mean, I hope I don't come across as cold or emotionless right now? I really try my best to be pleasant and responsive with everyone. Do I seem okay to you in that regard?

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is bizarre/impossible, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Is it possible in real life for your colleague to alter those records without IT being able to detect it?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because for months I’ve been seeing the same pattern in the project files—certain subcontractors and one colleague keep making tiny changes to the translation memory and timestamps so it looks like my quality control failed, and even when IT says the audit trail is clean, I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is challenging the patient's belief by asking about the plausibility of the colleague altering records without IT detecting it. This directly addresses the fixed nature of the belief despite contradictory evidence (IT saying the audit trail is clean), which is the core of the 'Delusions' symptom.

patient.answer:
Well, um, I know it sounds a bit... unusual, I suppose. And I really don't want to come across as difficult or, or paranoid—I know how that sounds. But yes, I do believe it's possible. 

I mean, I'm here because for months now, I've been seeing this same pattern in our project files. It’s just these tiny, tiny changes, you know? Certain subcontractors and this one colleague, they keep altering the translation memory and the timestamps. It's done in a way that makes it look like my quality control failed. And, well, even when IT says the audit trail is clean and they can't find anything, I just... I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. 

I really try to be a team player, I do, and I hate even bringing this up because I want to be easy to work with. But the pattern is just so clear to me. I hope I'm explaining this in a way that makes sense? I'm not trying to cause trouble, I just want to do my job well. Does that seem like a reasonable concern to have, given the circumstances?

doctor.intent: Determine whether there is any history of hallucinations in another sensory modality, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever seen things that other people could not see?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about visual hallucinations (seeing things other people cannot see). The symptom profiles do not include hallucinations (only delusions, additional requirement 1, functional impairment, and duration).

patient.answer:
Oh, no, definitely not. I've never had any... well, any hallucinations or anything like that. I know that's something doctors have to ask about, but I promise my eyes are perfectly fine. 

I mean, the things I'm noticing at work, they're right there on the screen in the files, you know? It's not something I'm just imagining or seeing out of nowhere. I've always had very good vision—I kind of have to, staring at documents all day. I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm seeing things that aren't there. I'm very grounded in reality, I really am. I hope that puts your mind at ease? I'm trying to be as honest and helpful as possible.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is bizarre/impossible, which best distinguishes delusional disorder from schizophrenia at this point.
doctor.question: Do you believe your colleague has any impossible or supernatural way of changing the records without IT being able to detect it?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient believes the colleague is using impossible or supernatural methods (bizarre delusions). The symptom profile describes the delusion (S019) but does not specify if the patient believes the methods are supernatural or bizarre, only that the patient believes the records are altered despite IT saying the audit trail is clean.

patient.answer:
Oh, no, no, nothing like that. Um, I don't believe in anything supernatural or... or impossible. I know how that might sound, and I really don't want you to think I'm losing touch with reality or anything. 

I just think they're very, very good with computers. Maybe they know a workaround or some sort of backdoor in the software that IT just hasn't caught onto yet? People figure out ways to get around firewalls and things all the time, right? It's just a technical thing, nothing magical. I really hope I'm not coming across as, well, crazy for thinking that? I'm just trying to make sense of what I'm seeing in the files in a logical way. Does that sound like a reasonable explanation to you?

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been any brief period of prominent psychotic symptoms beyond the single fixed work-related delusion, which would favor schizophrenia over delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a period when your thoughts felt jumbled or confused?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized thinking or confusion (symptoms of formal thought disorder or delirium), which is not covered by any of my symptom profiles (Delusions, Additional Requirement 1, Functional Impairment, Duration).

patient.answer:
Oh, um, no. No, my thoughts are usually very clear. I mean, I have to be sharp for my work, translating and keeping track of all the details. I don't really get confused or... or jumbled up. 

I mean, I might get a little stressed sometimes, like anyone would, especially with everything going on at the office right now. But my mind is working just fine, I promise. I really try to stay organized and focused. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to reassure you that I'm thinking completely straight.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the delusional belief is accompanied by Schneiderian/passivity phenomena that would support schizophrenia rather than delusional disorder.
doctor.question: Have you ever felt that someone was controlling your actions or movements?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about delusions of control (feeling that someone is controlling actions or movements), which is a specific type of bizarre delusion often associated with schizophrenia. My symptom profile includes non-bizarre delusions about colleagues altering files, but it does not include delusions of control. Therefore, I have no specific item for this.

patient.answer:
Oh, no, absolutely not. I... I've never felt like a puppet or anything like that. I'm always the one in charge of what I do. 

I know sometimes people with, um, mental health struggles might feel that way, but I promise I'm completely in control of my own actions. I make my own choices, go where I want to go, do what I need to do. It's just the files at work that are being messed with, not me. I wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my grip on myself. I'm very independent. Does that make sense? I hope I'm being helpful.

inference.note: Persistent, non-bizarre persecutory delusion limited to one work-related theme for 11 months with otherwise preserved functioning and no hallucinations, thought disorder, negative symptoms, passivity phenomena, or broader suspiciousness; this rules against F20.0 and supports delusional disorder.

opening_question.intent: Learn the patient's main concern or reason for seeking evaluation today
opening_question.question: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a single, persistent non-bizarre persecutory delusional belief focused on a colleague altering work records to make him appear at fault, maintained despite contrary evidence from IT. The belief has lasted about 11 months and is circumscribed rather than generalized. He denies hallucinations, thought control, disorganization, negative symptoms, neurological illness, and broader functional decline, which argues against schizophrenia-spectrum psychosis, mood disorder with psychotic features, or organic causes. This presentation is most consistent with persistent delusional disorder.
